## Schools Scramble for Alternatives as LPG Shortage Hits Mid-Day Meal Programs

Across India, schools are facing a growing crisis due to the ongoing shortage of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) used in mid-day meal programs.  While some rural areas rely on firewood and local stoves, many schools, especially those in urban centers, have been forced to cut back on their menus due to limited LPG supply. This has raised concerns about the nutritional quality of meals provided to children. 

Despite official restrictions only on commercial LPG supplies, school authorities are struggling to secure enough cylinders for their programs. The situation is particularly acute during exam seasons when student attendance drops and schools may close soon after exams.  In some states like Bihar, schools have switched to traditional earthen stoves using firewood and coal as a temporary solution while others rely on local resources or community kitchens.
